en.title: Gala del Sol Builds a Tropical Steampunk Universe With 'Rains Over Babel'
en.summary: Filmmaker Gala del Sol is expanding her vibrant, queer interpretation of Dante's Inferno into a larger universe. Her critically acclaimed debut, 'Rains Over Babel,' is more than just an awards contender; it's the launchpad for a bold new world.
en.body:
Prepare to be swept away by the electrifying vision of **Gala del Sol** and her debut feature, **Rains Over Babel**. This Colombian gem, already Colombia's official submission for the 99th Academy Awards, is a dazzling explosion of creativity that reimagines Dante's "Inferno" through a queer, tropical-punk lens. Set in the mythical City of Maya, a retrofuturistic version of Cali, Colombia, the film plunges audiences into a world of intersecting stories, from a deputy grim reaper paying off debts to a drag queen grappling with faith, all centered around a legendary dive bar called Babel.

The film's unique aesthetic, propelled by funky tropical music and a blend of magical and gritty realism, has captivated audiences and critics alike since its premiere at the Sundance Film Festival in 2025. **Gala del Sol**, a graduate of Chapman University, has crafted a narrative rich with love, identity, resilience, and the pursuit of second chances, all while breaking the fourth wall with charismatic narrators like the devil El Boticario and guardian angel Erato.

"For all the imagination that made it on screen in Rains Over Babel, there’s more where that came from in the mind of writer and director Gala del Sol," shared del Sol in a recent interview. This sentiment hints at the expansive ambitions behind her breakout film, which has already signed her with representation at M88.

## A Universe Born from Dreams

**Rains Over Babel** is more than just a film; it’s the genesis of an entire universe. Del Sol's inspiration reportedly stems from her own dreams, which she has meticulously translated onto screen. The film's success has fueled her desire to build upon this foundation, likening her plans to creating her own "Marvel universe." This suggests a future filled with interconnected stories and characters that will further explore the vibrant, gender-fluid world she has so vividly brought to life. The film itself is a cinematic love letter to Cali, reimagined as a mythical metropolis teeming with life and magic.

## The Appeal for Cult Fans

For avid readers and fans of unique storytelling, the prospect of a "tropical steampunk" universe is incredibly exciting. **Rains Over Babel** offers a refreshing departure from conventional narratives, blending familiar literary touchstones with bold, contemporary sensibilities. The film’s exploration of complex themes through a visually stunning and audaciously queer lens resonates deeply with a global audience hungry for diverse and original content. The potential for this universe to expand into other media, much like successful literary adaptations, is a thrilling prospect for those who appreciate intricate world-building and unforgettable characters.

## What's Next for Del Sol's World

While specific details about future projects within this burgeoning universe have not yet been announced, **Gala del Sol**'s clear vision and the international acclaim for **Rains Over Babel** indicate that this is just the beginning. Fans can eagerly anticipate further explorations of the City of Maya and its inhabitants, potentially through sequels, spin-offs, or other creative endeavors. The journey into del Sol's imaginative world has officially begun.

content_raw: Movies & TV Gala del Sol on Launching a Tropical Steampunk Universe with Rains Over Babel By Reuben Baron | Published on November 13, 2026 Comment 0 Share New Share Rains Over Babel &url= target=”_blank” title=”Twitter”> Rains Over Babel ” target=”_blank” title=”Pinterest”> Rains Over Babel , Colombia’s official submission for Best International Feature at the 99th Academy Awards, is a movie bursting with creativity. Describing the film as a queer Latin American twist on Dante’s Inferno only scratches the surface of what’s going on its many intersecting stories, which include a deputy grim reaper (Felipe Aguilar Rodriguez) scheming to pay off debts to his boss (Saray Rebolledo), a drag queen who might also be Jesus (William Hurtado) struggling with his preacher father (Jhon Narváez), and a mission to rescue a singer (Jacobo Vélez) from a hellish sex club. The devil El Boticario (Santiago Pineda) and guardian angel Erato (Sofia Buenaventura) serve as fourth wall-breaking narrators, guiding the audience into a journey that’s simultaneously campy and cool, heartfelt and bonkers, and not quite like anything you’ve seen before. For all the imagination that made it on screen in Rains Over Babel , there’s more where that came from in the mind of writer and director Gala del Sol. Speaking to Reactor as part of the film’s awards season press tour, Gala shared how she plans to turn this unexpected international success, drawn from her dreams, into the launching point for her own “Marvel universe.” Reuben Baron: I saw this movie at Sundance in 2025 and loved it. January 2025 was a very bad time for queer people in the U.S. so streaming this big joyous and crazy queer fantasy was a relief needed. Then I heard nothing about it for a while, but this spring it finally came out in Colombia and is now an official Oscar submission. What was the journey like going from that Sundance premiere to finally getting it released after so long? Gala del Sol: The whole of 2025, we did a festival circuit, so we showed the film at over 80 film festivals around the world and had theatrical distribution in 23 countries. Unfortunately, the U.S. was not one of them. As you said, it was a very hard time for queer people, crazy stuff going on in politics, and a lot of the distribution companies unfortunately were not interested in taking a risk on a film that was in Spanish and also queer. That’s double-niche! So we got a bunch of nos from the U.S., but we were able to show the film in theaters in over 23 countries, we sold it for HBO Max in Europe, FILMIN in Spain, and then finally we premiered in Colombia in April 16 of this year and we ran for 14 weeks in commercial theaters. That was a surprise for everyone, I think. The industry maybe has a limiting belief about the reach of LGBTQIA+ stories and I think we defied that.
